literal: Even having besieged, without besieging even having attacked, even causing treachery, to capture it is difficult, a fortress.
translation: A true fortress is one that is difficult to capture whether the enemy lays a complete siege, storms it directly, or attempts to breach it through treachery.
modern: பகைவர்கள் முற்றுகையிட்டாலும், முற்றுகையிடாமல் நேரடியாகத் தாக்கினாலும், உள்ளிருப்போரை வஞ்சித்துச் சதி செய்தாலும், கைப்பற்றுவதற்கு அரியதே சிறந்த அரணாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate resilience of a good fortress against various military tactics. It states that a fort must withstand a prolonged siege, a sudden direct assault, and internal treachery or breaches. The words 'முற்றியும்' (besieging), 'எறிந்தும்' (storming), and 'அறைப்படுத்தும்' (causing treachery) cover the three main ways an enemy might try to take a fort. A true fortress remains impenetrable and difficult to capture despite all these threats.
